Ten places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes in a
real Lakeshore document. The first four were checked and loading at the time this page was
written; the rest were added later and each carries its own verification note.

- **[21 CFR 11.10, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the full closed-system controls section this lesson quotes from: (d) access limits, (f)
  operational sequencing checks, (g) authority checks, (h) device checks, plus (a), (e), (i), (j),
  and (k) named but not re-taught here. Read it in full to see all eleven controls sitting together,
  not just the four this module spends its depth on.

- **[21 CFR 11.3, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.3)**
  — Part 11's definitions section, including closed system (b)(4) and open system (b)(9), the
  distinction this lesson's vendor-remote-access question turns on. Read the surrounding
  definitions too — "electronic record" and "electronic signature" are worth having exact before
  `data-integrity-and-records` builds further on them.

- **[FDA guidance page: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures — Scope and Application](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/part-11-electronic-records-electronic-signatures-scope-and-application)**
  — the 2003 guidance this lesson quotes for FDA's enforcement-discretion posture and its "we
  intend to enforce" list. Worth reading in full once: it's short, it's still the current guidance
  on this topic, and it explains its own reasoning for narrowing Part 11's scope, not just the
  bullet list this lesson pulled from it.

- **[FDA guidance page: Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's Facility](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)**
  — the same BECS guidance this course has used since module 1, the source for this lesson's
  training sentence (III.G) and remote-access-log recommendation (III.B). Worth rereading section
  III.B in full for the rest of its system-documentation list, which module 3 covered and this
  lesson only used the tail end of.

- **[Electronic Systems, Electronic Records, and Electronic Signatures Webinar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Im7TRkOS0mM)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson. FDA's own channel, on its Part 11 guidance for electronic systems in clinical
  investigations. Not blood- or BECS-specific, and not the 2003 scope guidance; watch it for FDA's
  framing of validation, access, and IT service providers. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA webinar slides: Electronic Systems, Electronic Records, and Electronic Signatures in Clinical Investigations](https://www.fda.gov/media/169688/download)**
  — the slide deck FDA's Office of Medical Policy presented for the draft version of that guidance
  (April 2023 presentation). Read it if you'd rather skim than watch; its overview lists
  electronic records, electronic systems, and IT service providers and services. It covers the
  draft, so check the final guidance below for the current wording. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA guidance page: Electronic Systems, Electronic Records, and Electronic Signatures in Clinical Investigations: Questions and Answers](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/electronic-systems-electronic-records-and-electronic-signatures-clinical-investigations-questions)**
  — the final guidance the webinar above explains. Clinical-investigation scope, so it doesn't
  govern a blood center, but it is current FDA writing on risk-based validation and on using
  outside service providers for electronic records, useful context for the vendor remote-access and
  hosting question. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR 211.68, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.68)**
  — the automatic, mechanical, and electronic equipment section that FDA's BECS guidance names as
  the predicate-rule basis for validation. Read it next to 11.10(a) to see why the lesson says the
  enforcement mechanism is the predicate rule. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2: Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Security](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/46/r2/final)**
  — a general IT-security guide to securing remote access, the ITSM side of this lesson's bridge
  (PAM, time-bound access, logged sessions). It isn't a Part 11 or FDA document; use it for how to
  engineer a vendor connection Lakeshore can grant, log, and revoke. Verified loading via `curl`
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE GAMP 5 Guide, Second Edition](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the publisher's page for the industry-practice framework from module 1. Its description
  emphasizes service providers and leveraging supplier documentation, relevant to how much weight a
  vendor's claims get. The guide itself is a paid publication; this page is the description only.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about audit trails, electronic records and data integrity.

- **[Audit Trail Review: Regulation and Practice in GxP Environments](https://ispe.org/pharmaceutical-engineering/march-april-2026/audit-trail-review-regulation-and-practice-gxp)** (ISPE, *Pharmaceutical Engineering*) — compares what regulators expect of audit trail review with what industry actually does. Practical background for audit-trail review procedures. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[What 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e) Actually Requires of an Audit Trail](https://ispe.org/pharmaceutical-engineering/ispeak/what-21-cfr-part-11-ss1110e-actually-requires-audit-trail-and-why)** (ISPE, ISPEAK opinion piece) — an author's argument about where common audit trail implementations fall short. An opinion piece; treat it as a viewpoint, not authority. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[GAMP Guide: Records & Data Integrity](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-records-pharmaceutical-data-integrity)** (ISPE) — the catalogue page for ISPE's data-integrity guide, showing what it covers. The guide itself is paid. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
